newsitem.title: TURKEY: NATO's Solana begins talks in Ankara.
newsitem.headline: NATO's Solana begins talks in Ankara.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana met Turkey's defence minister on Thursday at a start of a one-day visit to Ankara expected to focus on the country's tense relations with fellow NATO-member and neighbour Greece.
"I would publicly say that Turkey is playing a very very important role in NATO as it has in the past," Solana told reporters after meeting Defence Minister Turhan Tayan.
During his trip he will meet Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller and leading military officials before leaving Turkey on Thursday evening.

Solana is expected to address relations between fellow NATO members Turkey and Greece. His trip comes at a time of renewed tension over Cyprus, which plans to buy Russian missiles to counter Turkish aircraft. Turkey has threatened a military strike if they are installed.

As Solana began his talks, Turkish Cypriot and Greek Cypriot soldiers clashed in the buffer zone dividing Cyprus after the Greek Cypriots attempted to pull down a Turkish flag, Turkey's state-run Anatolian news agency said.
Two Greek Cypriots were killed in two similar incidents last year.
NATO officials fear conflict between the two members on its southern flank could harm plans to reform the alliance and take in new members from former communist east Europe.
Solana, who visited both countries last year, will urge Ankara to accept confidence-building measures. He is expected to visit Athens toward the end of the month.
Solana is also expected to discuss NATO expansion. Turkey has said the expansion of NATO was linked to the development of the EU and its defence wing, the Western European Union (WEU).

Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller has warned that Ankara could veto NATO's eastward expansion if its aspirations for closer ties with the EU remain frustrated. Turkey could also block plans to lend NATO equipment to the WEU, in which Ankara only has observer status.
Solana said ahead of his visit that he did not think Turkey would block anything.
